entry.title: Bessemer HPC will cease service on 31st October 2025

link.title: Bessemer HPC will cease service on 31st October 2025

entry.content:
This is an early notification that Bessemer will cease service at end of day on Friday 31st October 2025.

Action Required:

Transfer all needed data from /home and /fastdata to Stanage or to your research storage (see below).

Check if your required software is available on Stanage — raise a ticket if not.

Test workloads on Stanage.

Request /shared (Research Storage) access on Stanage via research-it@sheffield.ac.uk, confirming no sensitive data is stored there.

Note: /shared is not accessible on Stanage compute nodes — you must stage data via login nodes.

Onboarding sessions coming soon. Start planning your transition now.
entry.summary: This is an early notification that Bessemer will cease service at end of day on Friday 31st October 2025.

entry.title: Stanage downtime for maintenance: 30th June - 4th July 2025

link.title: Stanage downtime for maintenance: 30th June - 4th July 2025

entry.content:
From 30th June 2025, our High Performance Computing (HPC) platform, Stanage, will be unavailable for several days so that various important activities can be performed during a maintenance window.

Period of downtime for Stanage: From 08:00 on 30th June 2025 until 17:00 on 4th July 2025

We will try to minimise this downtime and it is possible that Stanage will return to service before 4th July. We will notify you by email when Stanage is back online and available for job submission.

Reason for this work:

  • Apply firmware and driver updates
  • Improve aspects of system resilience and power management
  • Expand the home directory area as it is reaching capacity
  • Upgrade the Slurm job scheduler

This work is necessary and we regret any disruption caused.

If you have any questions or concerns please get in touch via research-it@sheffield.ac.uk.
entry.summary: From 30th June 2025, our High Performance Computing (HPC) platform, Stanage, will be unavailable for several days so that various important activities can be performed during a maintenance window.

entry.title: Stanage cluster operating system and firmware upgrades

link.title: Stanage cluster operating system and firmware upgrades

entry.content:
Starting today, Thursday the 6th of March, the Stanage HPC nodes (including GPU nodes) will start to drain of jobs in order to reboot and apply operating system, kernel and omnipath network card updates.

Over the weeks following, decreases in capacity across the cluster is expected. The decreases in capacity are being mitigated by staggered drainage and reboot cycles for all nodes.

Nodes undergoing maintenance and the reason for the maintenance can be seen using the following command:

sinfo -R --format="%50E %N %.6t"

See the following link for further formatting options of the sinfo command: https://slurm.schedmd.com/sinfo.html#OPT_format
entry.summary: Starting today, Thursday the 6th of March, the Stanage HPC nodes (including GPU nodes) will start to drain of jobs in order to reboot and apply operating system, kernel and omnipath network card updates.

entry.title: Bessemer HPC system planned (non-disruptive) maintenance: Slurm scheduler upgrade - February 13, 2025 between 11:00 and 13:00

link.title: Bessemer HPC system planned (non-disruptive) maintenance: Slurm scheduler upgrade - February 13, 2025 between 11:00 and 13:00

entry.content:
An update is required for the Slurm scheduler (from 23.02.7 to 24.05.5) on the Bessemer HPC cluster. This maintenance is scheduled for February 13, 2025, between 11:00 to 13:00.

While this is a significant upgrade from 23.02.7 to 24.05.5, we do not anticipate any long-term disruption to users nor any major changes to SLURM behaviour. However, there will be very brief periods of command unavailability during the upgrade process.

Specifically:

  • sacct commands and other commands querying the Slurm database:
    • When the SLURM database service is restarting, these commands may get stuck or fail to complete.
    • This part of the upgrade will take approximately 60 seconds.
  • sbatch job submissions and sstat commands and other commands querying the Slurm controllers:
    • When the SLURM controllers are restarting, these commands may get stuck or fail to complete.
    • This part of the upgrade will take approximately 10 seconds.

When this maintenance is complete we will be in contact to confirm this is the case.

This maintenance has been organised under change ID: C2502 072

Update: This maintenance completed without issue.
entry.summary: An update is required for the Slurm scheduler (from 23.02.7 to 24.05.5) on the Bessemer HPC cluster. This maintenance is scheduled for February 13, 2025, between 11:00 to 13:00.

entry.title: Major HPC documentation update: New Stanage All Package Index launched!

link.title: Major HPC documentation update: New Stanage All Package Index launched!

entry.content:
We are excited to announce a major update to the HPC documentation: the launch of the All Package Index for the Stanage Software pages.

This comprehensive index includes all packages installed on Stanage, with content generated automatically. It is updated regularly to reflect the latest installations and mirrors the full range of packages available on Stanage.

Each package entry includes minimal documentation, providing key details such as descriptions, version information, dependencies for the latest version, URLs, and build log locations.

Explore the new documentation here:

https://docs.hpc.shef.ac.uk/en/latest/stanage/software/stacks/index.html
entry.summary: We are excited to announce a major update to the HPC documentation: the launch of the All Package Index for the Stanage Software pages.

entry.title: Stanage HPC cluster TOTP Multifactor authentication has been replaced with DUO Multifactor authentication

link.title: Stanage HPC cluster TOTP Multifactor authentication has been replaced with DUO Multifactor authentication

entry.content:
At 8am on 16th January we replaced the Stanage HPC cluster’s TOTP based multifactor authentication (MFA) with the University’s standard DUO MFA.

When users connect to Stanage they will now be prompted via a push notification to their DUO device to approve access or must enter a one-time code from their University provided hardware token which is associated with their DUO account.

  • Users connecting from workers nodes back to the login nodes may see a warning due to the now changed host key fingerprints. Users should check / amend such that their SSH client expects and gets the correct host key fingerprints as per: https://docs.hpc.shef.ac.uk/en/latest/FAQs.html#login-node-ssh-rsa-ecdsa-ed25519-host-key-fingerprints (i.e. amend their .ssh/known_hosts file).

  • Users making use of Filezilla will now need to follow the same instructions as required for the Bessemer cluster to avoid being prompted by MFA multiple times while transferring files: https://docs.hpc.shef.ac.uk/en/latest/FAQs.html#problems-connecting-with-filezilla-due-to-mfa

If there are any issues please get in touch via research-it@sheffield.ac.uk.
entry.summary: At 8am on 16th January we replaced the Stanage HPC cluster’s TOTP based multifactor authentication (MFA) with the University’s standard DUO MFA.

entry.title: Stanage and Bessemer GPU Driver updates - version 550.127.05 shortly available

link.title: Stanage and Bessemer GPU Driver updates - version 550.127.05 shortly available

entry.title: Stanage central software storage volume non-disruptive maintenance

link.title: Stanage central software storage volume non-disruptive maintenance

entry.content:
The storage volume used to provide the centrally provided software for users on Stanage is nearly full. Maintenance work to increase the capacity of this area is scheduled for November 5th between 10am and 11:30am.

This work is atypical and is expected to be non-disruptive to users and jobs on the cluster. Even so, during this period all jobs and interactive sessions using centrally provided software on Stanage should be considered at risk.

Rescheduled maintenance

Note: This work has been rescheduled to November 6th between 10am and 11:30am due to unexpected issues.
entry.summary: The storage volume used to provide the centrally provided software for users on Stanage is nearly full. Maintenance work to increase the capacity of this area is scheduled for November 5th between 10am and 11:30am.
